Ms. Indu Bala, Adv. for R-2
 alongwith R-2 in person.

Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anish Dayal

Order
% 20.03.2023 Crl.M.A. 7276/2023 (Exemption)
1. Exemption is allowed subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application is disposed of.

This petition has been filed for quashing of the FIR No.583/2017 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC at PS Narela, Delhi, on the ground that the parties have settled their disputes vide Settlement Deed dated 25.11.2022 with the facilitation of the Counselling Cell, the Family Courts,
Rohini, which is on record of this Court.

As per the settlement, a balance amount of Rs.2 Lakh is to be paid at this stage, to respondent No.2, which has been tendered vide a DD No.504870 dated 13.03.2023 for Rs.2,00,000/- drawn on ICICI Bank, Connaught Place Branch, New Delhi, and to respondent No.2, who has duly received and acknowledged the same.
2. Petitioner Nos.1 - 4 and respondent No.2/complainant are present in the Court, duly identified by the counsels and the IO.
Petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 15.05.2013.
No child was born out of the wedlock and due to difference between them, the marriage has resulted in a divorce vide decree dated 19.01.2023.

3. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State Sh Pradeep Kumar & Ors vs State & Anr on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54270627/
1 exchequer.
